title: Burst attenuator: queue decoupling with contextual trim scheduler
creator: Anika Rao
description: Problem: During cross-region failovers and short-lived traffic spikes we observe transient queue saturation that either increases p50/p95 latency beyond SLOs or triggers blunt circuit breakers that evict high-value tenants. Existing admission controllers focus on static priority lanes and token budgets; they react to occupancy but do not decouple ingress from execution fast enough for sub-30s bursts.
detailed_design: Introduce a new component called 'burst attenuator' that sits between the ingress router and the execution reservoir. Key behaviors: 1) queue decoupling: accept requests into a short-lived staging buffer with admission hints, immediately ACK-ing the caller with a soft-defer token when execution backlog is high; 2) contextual trim scheduler: evaluate each staged request against a trimming policy (tenant SLA score, request size in tokens, importance signals from request metadata) and apply targeted fidelity reduction (prefix trimming, function-call deferral, remove non-critical tool hooks, reduce max tokens) before dispatch; 3) graceful fallback paths: for requests that still cannot be scheduled within latency budget, route to cached completion, distilled single-sentence summary, or a low-cost model variant depending on tenant profile. The component exposes introspection metrics and per-tenant trace events for auditing and rollback.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: fast reaction to bursts without immediate eviction of reservations; preserves high-priority tenant SLOs by trimming less critical pieces of requests; reduces oscillation caused by blunt circuit breakers.
- Cons: increased complexity in runtime routing and billing alignment (we must track partial executions and downgraded responses); potential user-facing fidelity regressions if trimming heuristics are incorrect; introduces additional surface for correctness bugs (e.g., trimming tool calls might break structured APIs).
acceptance_criteria: Burst attenuator deployed behind a feature flag in one region (us-west-2) and processing live traffic in shadow mode
Metrics show reduced p95 latency spike magnitude during synthetic bursts by >=30% compared to baseline without attenuator
No customer-facing 50x error regressions in the experiment window; any degraded responses are labeled and countable in billing logs
Per-tenant fallback policy honors SLA tiers: gold tenants must not be routed to low-cost variant unless explicit consent flag set
End-to-end tracing from ingress->attenuator->execution appears in Console trace view and new dashboard panels
implementation_notes: Add staging buffer proto and ack token flow to ingress service (ingress-team) (Marcus)
Implement contextual trim engine with pluggable rules: tenant-score, token-cut, tool-suppression (runtime-team)
Integrate attenuator decisions with router and scheduler; expose metrics: staging_occupancy, trimmed_requests, fallback_routes, avg_trim_delta
Add billing annotation to record trimmed vs full executions for downstream cost reconciliation
Create a canary runbook with thresholds to auto-disable attenuator if error-rate or fidelity alerts cross safety limits

test_plan: Unit tests for trim rules and ack-token lifecycle
Integration tests: ingress -> attenuator -> scheduler with failure injection (simulate scheduler full / model OOM / region outage)
Chaos test: enable attenuator under CPU-starved node pool and validate auto-disable behaviour
Canary: launch at 1% traffic in us-west-2, monitor p50/p95, error-rate, trimmed_request_ratio for 72h before scale-up
rollout_plan: Phase A (shadow): run attenuator decisions in shadow mode for 1 week and generate dashboard baselines
Phase B (canary): enable feature flag for 1% traffic in us-west-2 for 72h, evaluate acceptance criteria
Phase C (regional): expand to 10% then 50% traffic with staged increases and SRE gate checks
Phase D (multi-region): after 2 regional successes, enable cross-region coordination so attenuator hints carry tenant scores across failover boundaries
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect trimming breaks structured outputs. Mitigation: conservative default rules (never strip required JSON fields) and opt-in for aggressive trims.
Risk: billing ambiguity for partial executions. Mitigation: annotated billing records and a reconciliation job in billing pipeline.
Risk: increased operational complexity. Mitigation: centralize rules in a single service with a safe ruleset and provide lightweight UI for overrides in Console
